question.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\sqrt{3},-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩, \\ N(t) & =⟨0,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\sqrt{3},-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\times ⟨0,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \sqrt{3} & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t & \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡t & \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨({sin}^{2}⁡t-(-{cos}^{2}⁡t)),-(-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t-0),(-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-0)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨1,\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
